files.role: Public single-fragment deletion set, visible-ordinal-to-physical-offset mapper, representation/conversion/iteration traits and parameterized local tests. It defines in-memory representations rather than deletion-file IO.
ranges: SPDX metadata and imports for HashSet<u32>, half-open Range, Arc ownership, core memory sizing, Arrow BooleanArray and RoaringBitmap. These imports establish that offsets are local u32 values, not stable u64 row IDs.

Private BITMAP_THRESDHOLD (spelling preserved) is usize 5_000; a TODO requests benchmarking rather than claiming the number is optimal. Public DeletionVector derives Debug, Clone and Default, with NoDeletions as default plus public Set(HashSet<u32>) and Bitmap(RoaringBitmap) variants. Direct callers can construct empty/nonempty variants without normalization or threshold enforcement.

DeepSizeOf children return zero for NoDeletions, delegate Set to its context-aware HashSet estimate, and use bitmap.serialized_size() for Bitmap. The latter is explicitly marked inexact; serialized bytes are not exact heap-allocation measurement. Inline enum size comes from the trait default. HashSet formula/default are at rust/lance-core/src/deepsize.rs:38-44 and rust/lance-core/src/deepsize.rs:213-220.

len selects zero, HashSet len or bitmap len cast to usize; is_empty uses len==0, independent of representation. contains performs false/set/bitmap membership. contains_range accepts Range<u32>, returning range.is_empty for NoDeletions, all set memberships for Set, or delegated bitmap containment. Set iterates every offset in the requested range, not just stored deletions; empty/reversed ranges are vacuously covered in the explicit range-iteration branches.

Private range_cardinality returns zero, folds across every requested offset accumulating HashSet membership as u64, or delegates to bitmap cardinality. Set cost therefore grows with the width of the queried offset range even when the set is small. Public iter returns a boxed Send iterator borrowed from self: empty, copied HashSet iterator, or bitmap iterator. Set order is unspecified; this method is not the sorted-iterator API.

into_sorted_iter consumes self and returns a boxed Send static iterator. Set collects into Vec, sorts, then returns owning iteration; Bitmap uses its already-sorted iterator per source comment. to_sorted_iter borrows self but clones the entire Set variant before calling into_sorted_iter, while Bitmap stays borrowed. Comments assume sets are small, but the public Set variant allows bypassing that assumption.

build_predicate receives slice::Iter<u64>. Bitmap/Set compute !contains(id as u32) for every address into Vec<bool>, then convert to BooleanArray: true means retain/not deleted, false deleted, and values are non-null. Casting discards the high fragment half, so callers must apply the single-fragment deletion vector to the correct fragment. NoDeletions returns None, but an empty Set/Bitmap returns Some(all true), including Some(empty) on empty input. This is not a fragment-ID validator or a stable-row-ID remapper.

OffsetMapper maps a zero-based visible-row ordinal to an undeleted local physical offset: deleting [0,1,2] yields 0->3,1->4,2->5. Documentation requires monotonically increasing inputs and says state is reused. Public struct holds private Arc<DeletionVector>, left search bound and last_diff; new initializes both cached u32 numbers to zero. There is no fragment physical-row-count field or total-row bound.

map_offset starts mid=offset+last_diff and right=offset+deletion count cast to u32. Each loop counts deleted offsets in 0..mid+1 and compares mid with offset+deleted_count. Equality with an undeleted mid stores last_diff=mid-offset and returns. Less asserts left!=mid+1, advances left=mid+1, then bisects [left,right]; greater or equality at a deleted mid moves right=mid and bisects. The comment explains leftward search for an overshooting guess. left persists across calls and is not reset on success; input monotonicity is not checked. Additions, subtraction, mid+1 and cardinality cast have no checked-error path, so near-u32-limit inputs can overflow under checked arithmetic or wrap otherwise. No validation rejects ordinals past actual fragment rows because that length is absent. With Set, every range-cardinality step scans 0..mid+1, a potentially large cost unrelated to set cardinality.

From<&DeletionVector> for RoaringBitmap clones a Bitmap, constructs from Set references, or creates a new empty bitmap for NoDeletions. It does not mutate the deletion vector or preserve its representation in the returned value.

PartialEq compares matching variants by contents; Set versus Bitmap collects the Set into a temporary RoaringBitmap and compares. NoDeletions equals only itself, so it differs from an empty Set or empty Bitmap even though all have len zero. Empty Set and empty Bitmap compare equal to each other. No Eq implementation is declared. Cross-representation comparison allocates a temporary bitmap.

Extend<u32> first converts its argument into an iterator, then mem::take(self) installs default NoDeletions while matching the old variant and iterator size_hint. For old NoDeletions, upper bound Some(0) preserves it without consuming items; lower>=5000 selects Bitmap directly; otherwise a known upper<5000 selects Set. These decisions use item-count bounds, not eventual distinct cardinality, so many duplicate inputs can select a bitmap with few distinct offsets. The comment says mem::replace, while the actual call is mem::take.

For unknown/ambiguous size when old NoDeletions, collect a Set and promote only if distinct len>5000. Existing Set also extends then promotes strictly above 5000; existing Bitmap never demotes. Hence exactly 5000 unique items with a lower bound of 5000 become Bitmap, but the same unique count with insufficient size-hint information or an existing Set can stay Set. An unknown-size empty iterator can create Set(empty). Panics after mem::take (including iterator/hash/allocation operations) do not restore the previous vector: self remains default until the final assignment succeeds.

A TODO sketches get and BitAnd APIs as comments only. IntoIterator has Item=u32 and boxed Send IntoIter; it returns empty, or sorts Set values in an owned Vec, or takes bitmap iteration. Thus consuming IntoIterator is sorted, unlike borrowed iter. The comment claims Set is guaranteed small, but direct public construction and the iterator-hint rules do not enforce such a global bound.

FromIterator<u32> constructs default then delegates to Extend, inheriting representation/size-hint behavior. From<RoaringBitmap> normalizes an empty bitmap to NoDeletions and otherwise preserves Bitmap even when small. This normalization differs from direct Bitmap construction and extending an existing empty Bitmap.

The cfg(test) module is coverage-excluded as a whole and imports rstest. Helpers set_dv/bitmap_dv deliberately construct exact variants. test_set_bitmap_equality compares 0..100 across representations. test_threshold_promotes_to_bitmap collects exact-size 0..5000 and asserts Bitmap; it does not test the unknown-hint exactly-5000 branch.

rstest test_map_offsets covers middle deletions [3,5] and leading [0,1,2], mapping ascending ordinals to expected kept rows. test_deep_size_of requires NoDeletions equal inline enum size and nonempty Set/Bitmap estimates greater than inline size. It does not establish exact bitmap allocation accounting.

Parameterized test_len_is_empty checks NoDeletions zero/true, Set three/false, Bitmap five/false. test_contains checks NoDeletions false plus present/missing offsets for both stored forms. No explicit empty stored variant case appears here.

test_contains_range covers empty/nonempty NoDeletions and fully covered/partially missing ranges for both Set and Bitmap. test_range_cardinality checks zero for NoDeletions and bitmap counts three over 0..20, one over 6..14. It does not directly test Set range_cardinality or reversed ranges.

test_iterators parameterizes all three variants. It sorts borrowed iter output before comparison (so does not require Set iteration order), but directly compares to_sorted_iter, cloned into_sorted_iter and consuming into_iter with ascending expected values.

test_build_predicate uses addresses 0..4. NoDeletions gives None; Set[1,3] gives true/false/true/false/true; Bitmap[0,2,4] gives false/true/false/true/false. Unwrapping each BooleanArray item confirms no nulls for these fixtures. It does not test mixed fragment high bits or empty stored variants.

test_to_roaring checks output lengths for all three input variants, not every element. test_partial_eq checks same-form content equality, Set/Bitmap symmetry and NoDeletions versus nonempty forms. It omits comparisons between NoDeletions and empty Set/Bitmap.

test_extend checks exact empty stays NoDeletions, unknown-size ten-item source creates Set, filtered 10_000 creates Bitmap, small existing Set remains Set with six items, larger extension promotes it, and existing Bitmap remains Bitmap with six. It does not cover duplicate-heavy hints, unknown-hint exactly5000 or unwind after taking self.
test_from_roaring asserts empty normalization to NoDeletions and a three-item bitmap remains Bitmap, consistent with conversion rather than size-threshold minimization.

test_map_offset_dense_then_sparse deletes four of five rows in 0..500 and one of five in 500..1000, explicitly stores Bitmap, and checks visible offsets 0->0,1->5,99->495,100->501. It covers a density transition with sparse calls, not all visible rows, decreasing input, exhaustion or u32 boundaries. All tests were read, not executed.
files.limits: This file does not read/write .arrow/.bin deletion files, choose a persisted deletion format or validate a fragment length. Legacy/current storage emission cannot be inferred from the Set/Bitmap enum alone. Predicate fragment correctness and monotonic OffsetMapper use are caller responsibilities to trace later. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/deletion.rs:14-21; rust/lance-core/src/utils/deletion.rs:104-183)

files.role: Public MappingReader contract and OrderedCompactionMapping adapter for one rewrite group. Graph traversal and index/manifest orchestration are explicitly outside this file.
ranges: SPDX and module docs place graph traversal in the FRI reader. Imports bring shared Arc ownership, async_trait expansion, RowAddrRemap, core deep-size context/trait and Error/Result. FRI expansion and RowAddrRemap algorithm are not defined by these imports.

Public async-trait MappingReader requires Send+Sync+Debug+DeepSizeOf. Despite row_id names, the contract explicitly says physical addresses. remap_row_id(&self,u64)->Result<Option<u64>> returns mapped address or None for deleted source row; addresses outside source fragments or outside their valid offset ranges must return InvalidInput. Persisted invalid mappings should produce CorruptFile and storage errors propagate. These error requirements are an interface contract; the trait cannot enforce every implementation.

Default remap_row_ids(&self,&[u64])->Result<Vec<Option<u64>>> reserves input length, iterates in input order and sequentially awaits remap_row_id, pushing one result per input. Duplicates and None positions are preserved, empty input gives empty Vec, and the first Err stops iteration and discards the partial result. There is no concurrent buffering or aggregation. Cancellation can interrupt an in-flight single-row future; the trait makes no rollback promise for implementation side effects.

OrderedCompactionMapping derives Debug and privately owns Arc<RowAddrRemap>. Documentation calls it an adapter for one group's existing bitmap/rank remap, explicitly not replacing the legacy FRI reader or writer. Public new simply stores the Arc; its documentation presumes fragment layout validation happened when the remap was constructed, and no additional validation is performed here.

Private map_row_id invokes remap.get(row_id).ok_or_else with an InvalidInput message containing the full u64 row ID when the outer Option is absent. Present inner None passes through as deleted; present Some(address) passes through as mapped. DeepSizeOf delegates to the Arc remap children with the same Context, inheriting Arc dedup (rust/lance-core/src/deepsize.rs:182-190). The remap's own memory calculation and validation remain pending.

The async-trait implementation overrides both operations. Single maps synchronously through map_row_id; batch maps the borrowed slice through that helper and collects Result<Vec<Option<u64>>>. It avoids per-item async awaits and preserves order/duplicates; collect short-circuits on the first error. There is no internal await/yield or IO in these adapter bodies, though the interface is async.

Private cfg(test) imports RowAddress, GroupInputWithLayout and RoaringTreemap. Unit SingleRowReader derives Debug/DeepSizeOf and implements only single-row mapping: u64::MAX returns InvalidInput, zero gives None, others echo Some(row_id). It therefore exercises the trait default batch implementation rather than the adapter override.

Tokio test default_batch_preserves_positions_and_propagates_errors expects [2,0,1,2] -> [Some(2),None,Some(1),Some(2)], checks empty input, then [1,u64::MAX] produces InvalidInput with the precise test-message substring. It checks error category/text, not cancellation or post-error side effects.

The ordered-compaction test constructs a real RowAddrRemap through compact_with_layout: source fragments (1,3 rows),(2,1 row), surviving addresses (1,0),(1,2),(2,0), destination fragments (3,2 rows),(4,1 row). Its input is (2,0),(1,1),(1,0),(1,0), covering out-of-source-order requests, deletion and duplicate. Expected results are computed from remap.get and both batch and singles must equal them. This is an adapter-equivalence test, not an independent expected-address oracle for the underlying remap algorithm.

The same test checks empty batch and both absent fragment (99,0) and out-of-range offset (1,3). Each must error through single and batch calls with InvalidInput and message containing outside compaction mapping. No CorruptFile/storage-error path is exercised by this adapter fixture. Tests were read, not run.
files.limits: This public interface reads a single rewrite mapping and explicitly excludes FRI graph traversal/legacy replacement. The adapter's RowAddrRemap dependency and how callers select mapping chains remain pending; do not use this file alone to claim full compaction or stable-ID semantics. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/fragment_reuse.rs:4-4; rust/lance-core/src/utils/fragment_reuse.rs:14-73)
